title: Ansel and the Orchard
premise: In the final winter of the Vessarine Republic, Sebastian Underhill serves as a courier in a diplomatic delegation sent to negotiate with the rival kingdom of Ostrava, carrying sealed codes and keeping her identity as a woman hidden. When an Ostravan officer named Ansel arrives bearing letters in the handwriting of her presumed-dead brother, she learns he survived the war and lives under Ostravan protection—but only if the Republic falls. Torn between duty to a dying state and a promise made to her brother years ago, Sebastian must smuggle Ansel's proof of life past her own suspicious superiors, who begin hunting a traitor within the delegation. In the end, the armistice fails and the Republic collapses, but Sebastian chooses exile over loyalty, delivering the letters at terrible personal cost and finding, in the ruins of both nations, an unexpected belonging with Ansel.
about_author: Xanthe Iversen is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing diplomatic correspondence from collapsed states before turning to fiction. She writes from a farmhouse orchard, where she claims every tree has a story it refuses to tell.

chapters.title: The Last Dispatch
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The delegation departs the capital of the crumbling Vessarine Republic; Sebastian hides her gender behind courier's drudgery and memorizes the codebook she carries against her ribs. The beat is quiet dread: everyone pretends this mission matters.

chapters.title: Snow on the Border Road
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The convoy crosses into contested territory; she observes the delegation's fractious ministers and notes which guards are loyal to whom. A checkpoint search nearly exposes her. Emotional beat: the cost of invisibility—safety bought with erasure.

chapters.title: The Orchard at Vell
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The delegation quarters at a half-abandoned estate with a frozen orchard, where Sebastian tends the trees out of habit and homesickness. Flashback to her brother Tomas teaching her grafting. Beat: tenderness as armor.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Gate
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Ansel, an Ostravan officer under a flag of parley, arrives requesting the delegation's archivist—her. He produces letters in Tomas's unmistakable hand. Beat: shock that cracks her carefully maintained anonymity wide open.

chapters.title: Handwriting of the Dead
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, night. Alone, she verifies the letters: private jokes, a childhood scar, grafting terminology only Tomas knew. Her brother lives—and his survival depends on Ostrava's victory. Beat: grief inverted into hope, then guilt.

chapters.title: Terms of Parley
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel negotiates with the Republic's ministers, playing for time while privately assessing Sebastian as the only honest person in the room. He reveals nothing of the letters. Beat: his loneliness mirrors hers; two professionals recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Ministers Want
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Minister Corvane, ambitious and ruthless, begins consolidating control of the delegation's secrets—including suspicion of a leak. Sebastian realizes the codes she carries could buy Tomas's safety or seal her execution. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Promise in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Extended flashback, Sebastian's POV. Years earlier, she promised Tomas she would find him if war ever separated them, sealing the vow with grafted cuttings from their family orchard. Beat: understanding that promises outlive the governments that interrupt them.

chapters.title: Second Meeting, First Truth
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel and Sebastian meet secretly in the orchard; he explains Tomas defected to save his family and now lives under Ostravan protection, silenced unless the Republic falls. Beat: the first honest conversation either has had in years.

chapters.title: Corvane's Net
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Corvane intercepts a routine dispatch and finds evidence of unauthorized contact; he begins quietly interrogating staff. Sebastian burns one letter and memorizes the rest. Beat: paranoia closing in, trust becoming currency.

chapters.title: The Armistice Table
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Formal talks open at Vell; both sides posture while winter deepens. Sebastian transcribes coded minutes and realizes Corvane intends to sabotage the peace to seize power in the collapse. Beat: disillusionment—the enemy across the table is not the true enemy.

chapters.title: Cuttings
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She grafts cuttings from the estate orchard as a message only Tomas would understand, planning to send them via Ansel. A near-discovery by a guard forces Ansel to cover for her. Beat: love beginning to take root where duty is rotting.

chapters.title: An Arrest in the Night
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Corvane's men seize a junior clerk suspected of leaking; the man is innocent but breaks under questioning and names 'the courier.' Ansel warns Sebastian through a planted book. Beat: terror, and the realization she can no longer stay invisible.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Frozen Rows
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Cornered, Sebastian flees into the orchard; Ansel extracts her toward Ostravan lines. She abandons the official codes deliberately, taking only Tomas's letters. Beat: the irrevocable choice—she is now a traitor to everything but her promise.

chapters.title: Enemy Territory
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Crossing into Ostrava, she sees the war from the other side: conscripted villages, propaganda, ordinary grief identical to home's. Beat: belonging revealed as something people build, not something borders grant.

chapters.title: Corvane Ascendant
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV (only chapter). Back at Vell, Corvane frames the clerk's death on foreign agents, seizes the delegation, and prepares to sell the Republic's remnants to the highest bidder. Beat: cold clarity of ambition; power shown corrupting without remorse.

chapters.title: The Proof of Life
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel brings Sebastian to the garrison where Tomas is held under protective custody; the reunion is joyful and bruised—Tomas is changed, complicit, ashamed. Beat: the promise kept is not the promise imagined.

chapters.title: What Tomas Chose
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Tomas confesses he traded intelligence for his life and asks Sebastian to help him disappear entirely. She must decide whether love means absolution. Beat: forgiveness as a deliberate act, not a feeling.

chapters.title: The Fall of Vell
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. News arrives: the capital has fallen; Corvane's faction surrenders the Republic piece by piece while enriching itself. The armistice dies. Beat: catastrophe rendered intimate—the end of a nation experienced as the end of a version of oneself.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. To secure safe passage for Tomas, Sebastian offers Ostrava's spymasters the one thing she kept back: knowledge of Corvane's hidden accounts, ensuring his ruin. Beat: reclaiming power from a corrupt man by spending her last secret.

chapters.title: Spring Grafting
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. In a border village, Sebastian, Ansel, and Tomas plant the orchard cuttings she carried through everything. No nation claims them; they claim each other. Beat: quiet climax of belonging—roots chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Ansel and the Orchard
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, epilogue. Years later, a traveler asks the woman pruning trees whether she mourns the Republic. She answers that she mourns what it might have been, and prunes anyway. Beat: resolution—love against duty resolved into a life built from both losses.
